# Dane Malenfant

> Dane Malenfant is a machine learning researcher studying multi-agent reinforcement learning, reciprocity, temporal credit assignment, continual learning, and AI safety.

Dane completed an MSc in Computer Science at McGill University and conducted the research at Mila – The Québec AI Institute in the Learning in Neural Circuits Lab. The canonical website is [danemalenfant.com]({{ site.url }}/).

## Selected research

- [The Challenge of Hidden Gifts in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning]({{ site.url }}/publications/#hidden-gifts-title): Reciprocal behaviour when helpful actions have delayed or difficult-to-observe benefits; RLC 2026.
- [Contrastive Retrospection: honing in on critical steps for rapid learning and generalization in RL]({{ site.url }}/publications/#conspec-title): Contrastive identification of critical states for reinforcement learning; NeurIPS 2023.
- [Moral Hazard in Multi-Agent Language Models]({{ site.url }}/publications/#moral-hazard-title): Cooperation when information gathering is costly, hidden, and benefits another language agent; COLM 2026 workshop.
- [Compositional Flow Matching with Factored Velocity Fields]({{ site.url }}/publications/#factored-flow-title): Zero-shot generalization to unseen combinations of generative factors; ICML 2026 workshop spotlight.
- [Reinforcing the World's Edge]({{ site.url }}/publications/#worlds-edge-title): Continual learning at the boundary between multiple adaptive agents; World Modeling Workshop 2026.
- [Inconsistencies in Artificial Intelligence Strategy Alignment of NATO Member States]({{ site.url }}/publications/#nato-policy-title): Comparative analysis of public national and military AI strategies; 2024.
- [Causality Mining in Fiction]({{ site.url }}/publications/#causality-fiction-title): Causal-relation extraction and domain differences in literary fiction; Text2Story 2022.
